hypothesis: Add a video-side historical engagement-quality feature: a smoothed, leave-one-out long_view rate per video computed only from train-split history (Bayesian-smoothed with a population prior, exactly as run_pop already does for its own scoring, but exposed here as an input *feature* to the FM instead of a standalone score), bucketed into deciles as a new categorical field. This gives the FM an informative, low-variance prior for videos with few train interactions — where the sparse video_id embedding alone is noisy and prone to memorization/overfitting — which should directly help intra-user ranking quality by better discriminating video quality for less-seen items. Note this differs in mechanism from iter 1's rejected feature (which added static USER-profile categorical fields, providing no within-user discriminative signal); this is an ITEM-side signal that varies across a user's candidate set and so can actually move ranking.
reflection: The l2 sweep produced monotonically worse scores as l2 increased (0.6041→0.6038→0.6030→0.6019), with 1e-6 (unchanged default) winning — meaning stronger weight decay wasn't the fix for the post-peak degradation; the overfitting is likely driven by sparse embeddings memorizing specific (user,video) pairs rather than by raw weight magnitude, so a regularization-strength knob was the wrong lever entirely.
expected_effect: nDCG@5 should move more than GAUC, since this feature directly differentiates among the small set of items a user could see (improving top-of-list precision for sparse/cold videos), whereas GAUC integrates ranking correctness across the user's whole history where the video_id embedding already captures most signal for well-observed videos.
